text.p: Israeli bonds closed mixed on Tuesday with prices for unlinked bonds rising due to expectations of lower inflation, traders said.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: -0.1 pct to 168.42
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 165.64
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 157.58
"There was heavy demand for unlinked bonds and Makams because of expectations for a low September CPI," Boaz Leviathan, analyst at Sahar Securities, said. "Prices of CPI-linked bonds were stable."
September's CPI will be published on October 15.

Leviathan said the stability in CPI-linked bonds was a reaction to the sharp price rises of the past weeks. "The market is calmer, this is a more natural situation. The market may remain stable in the coming days, but it seems to be doing well," he said.

He said the bond market's recovery since its August crisis was mainly because the government had practically stopped issuing CPI-linked bonds. Provident funds had started buying bonds again, he added, after dumping them to meet massive public redemptions in July and August.

Israel's Treasury said on Tuesday that initial estimates pointed a significant decrease in public redemptions from the provident funds in October. Net redemptions in September totalled a huge 3.511 billion shekels.

Dan Scharia of Capital Investments said the mixed trading in CPI-linked bonds was a correction to the price rises of the past month. "Prices of short- and medium-term CPI-linked bonds fell a bit while prices in long-term bonds continued to rise but on a lesser scale," he said.
Note: Provident funds, long-term savings funds with tax benefits, had been dumping bonds in July and August to meet massive public redemptions.
Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
